texts.preamble: The Food Inspector, Rep.By P.P., ... vs G. Ramesh, Hyderabad, And 7 Otrs. on 5 June, 2023
texts.facts: Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 30.12.1999, P.W.1 inspected the premises of A-1 and found 49 kgs. of 'moongdal' in a loose gunny bag kept for sale to public for human consumption. Having served notice in accordance with the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, samples were drawn and sent for analysis on 31.12.1999. Having obtained the public analyst report, on the basis of the report of the Director, complaint was filed by P.W.1/Food Inspector. During the course of trial, learned Magistrate examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and marked Ex.P.1 to P.45. 3. The main ground on which the acquittal was recorded is that the accused had lost opportunity of sending the second sample drawn during the search to Central Food Laboratory (C.F.L.) in view of the delay in lodging the complaint. According to the learned Magistrate, there was a delay of more than two years in filing the complaint. Since the accused have lost their opportunity, the learned Magistrate found that the accused are entitled for acquittal.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the State would submit that there are valid grounds to interfere with the orders of acquittal.
